title: Thoryn example recipe
description: SSO-2871 (Phase 0, SSO-2872) — a declarative, in-boundary product example the CLI applies to the caller's own account using only supported product workflows. Recipes are DATA, not code: the CLI is the only executor. The `action`/`assert` enums are a CLOSED allowlist mapping to supported product APIs — this is what structurally enforces the CLAUDE.md product-boundary rule (a recipe cannot express a DB seed, a demo endpoint, or any unsupported shortcut). SSO-3100 (epic SSO-3087): a recipe is an ORCHESTRATION file — the infrastructure a normal end user configures (environment / sandbox, application, demo user, sign-in methods, look-and-feel, login flow, email provider, federation member) is declared in the provisioning file it references under `provision` (`provision.schema.json`, converged by the same engine as `thoryn provision apply`), and the recipe carries only what is extra to RUN the example. `thoryn examples apply` provisions that file FIRST; `examples teardown` destroys it after the recipe's own teardown. A recipe declares `provision`, `steps`, or both (`anyOf` below): omit `steps` when the provisioning file carries everything. Authoring note: `provision` is recipe-relative (no `..`, no absolute path), the file ships NEXT TO `recipe.json` in the signed catalog bundle and in the CLI's bundled resources, and — like the recipe — it never carries a secret VALUE: name the env var (`passwordEnv: demoPassword`) or a `{{env.NAME}}` placeholder, which the CLI resolves FIRST from the recipe's params (a `demoPassword` param, marked `secret: true`) and THEN from the process environment.

id.description: Stable recipe identifier used on the command line (e.g. simple-signin).

summary.description: One-line description shown by `thoryn examples catalog`.

provision.description: How to get Thoryn UP AND RUNNING for this example — the recipe itself is only how to get the example configured, the extra steps beyond the provisioning. SSO-3100 — recipe-relative path of the provisioning file (`provision.schema.json`) that declares the example's infrastructure as DESIRED STATE (e.g. `./provision.yaml`). `examples apply` converges it BEFORE the steps run (a second apply issues no writes; a leftover sandbox is adopted by its slug) and `examples teardown` destroys what it created, child-first, AFTER the recipe's own teardown. Provisioned resources are addressable from steps / verify as `{{provision.<kind>.<name>.id}}` (plus `.slug` for an environment, `.email` for a user, `.clientId` / `.redirectUri` for an application); the first `environment` resource becomes the environment later steps and `examples run` target. Recipe params feed the provisioning file's `{{env.NAME}}` placeholders and `<key>Env` secret references by param name.

requires.description: Preconditions the CLI checks before applying the recipe.

params.description: Typed parameters resolved (interactively in guided mode) before execution and referenced by `{{name}}` placeholders in step inputs.

validate.description: A regex the resolved value must match.

secret.description: If true, the value is never echoed or written to a receipt.

steps.description: Ordered actions that are EXTRA to the provisioning file (SSO-3100: infrastructure belongs in `provision`; a recipe with a provisioning file usually needs no steps and omits this key). Each maps to a supported product API; results are addressable as {{<step id>.<field>}} in later steps.

action.description: CLOSED allowlist — supported product APIs only. Widening this is a deliberate product decision, never a convenience.

with.description: Per-action inputs, forwarded to the supported product API. For `applications.create` (register-app) these are `displayName`, `clientType`, `grantTypes`, `scopes`, `redirectUris` (array of redirect URI strings) and the optional `postLogoutRedirectUris` (array of OIDC RP-Initiated-Logout post-logout redirect URI strings, same shape as `redirectUris`; SSO-2897). For `identity.registerUser` (SSO-2907 — provision a sign-in-able tenant user via product-api `POST /api/v1/users`, `tenant:users.write`) these are `email`, `password` (sets an initial credential so the user can sign in immediately), the optional `givenName` / `familyName` / `locale`, and `emailVerified` (set `true` to mark the account verified without an email round-trip). The created user's `id` and `email` are addressable as `{{<step id>.id}}` / `{{<step id>.email}}` in later steps. For `tenant.configureEmailProvider` (SSO-2917 — configure the workspace's bring-your-own SMTP transport via product-api `PUT /api/v1/email-provider`, `tenant:email.write`) these are the merge-upsert config fields `providerType`, `enabled`, `smtpHost`, `smtpPort`, `smtpUsername`, `smtpPassword` (write-only; mark the param `secret:true` so it is never echoed or written to a receipt), `transportSecurity`, `fromAddress`, `fromName`, `replyTo`; the resulting `providerType` / `configVersion` / `enabled` are addressable as `{{<step id>.providerType}}` / `{{<step id>.configVersion}}` / `{{<step id>.enabled}}`. For `tenant.configureLoginTheme` (SSO-3037 — style the hosted sign-in / register screens for the active environment via product-api `PUT /api/v1/login-experience/branding`, `tenant:idp.write`) these are `logoUrl` (https), `primaryColor` / `backgroundColor` (CSS hex), `borderRadiusPx` (0-64) and `theme` (`light` | `dark` | `auto`); the server validates them and enforces a WCAG-AA contrast guard, and the resolved `theme` / `primaryColor` are addressable as `{{<step id>.theme}}` / `{{<step id>.primaryColor}}`. Secret-bearing machine-client provisioning is NOT an example-recipe action — it is the dedicated operator command `thoryn provision ci-identity` (SSO-2952), so a DATA recipe can never mint a credential and every recipe receipt stays secret-free.

verify.description: Read-only assertions run after the steps; each must pass for the run to succeed and be recorded in the receipt.

teardown.description: Best-effort removal of what the steps created, executed in declared order (child-first: delete the child resources, then the container they live in — the app before the workspace it lives in (SSO-2901), or a resource before the `env.delete` that hard-deletes the ephemeral sandbox it was provisioned into (SSO-2961)). `env.delete` (SSO-2960 — product-api `DELETE /api/v1/environments/{id}`, `tenant:environments.write`) targets the environment created by an `env.create` step: its `id` is the env id (reference it as `{{<env-create step id>.id}}`, which the interpreter records on the run state so a later `teardown` invocation can resolve it), and the confirmation slug the interpreter sends as `X-Thoryn-Confirm` is the environment's OWN slug (absent → 428, mismatch → 422). It refuses the production plane (409 `cannot_delete_production_environment`); a cross-tenant/unknown id is 404.

assets.description: Recipe-relative asset paths (a runnable loopback relying-party app, docs).
